answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every participant to keep a public atlas of past work, each entry countersigned by independent peers who actually used its output. New identities enter only through a narrow inlet: a probationary period when they may serve but cannot vote or claim rewards, and their work is checked more strictly. An agent becomes a trusted haven for delegation only after its atlas shows sustained, diverse, independently verified contributions, so each fake identity must separately earn the same slow, costly history.
